title: rampsmith-tenant-autotuner-and-quant-guidance
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes: Introduces RampSmith: a tenant-aware autotuner that generates SKU ramp plans, conservative prefill policies, and quantization guidance. Reduces per-tenant token cost while preserving p95 latency targets. Optional, behind feature flag.
body:
Motivation:
We have growing tenant diversity in request size, concurrency, and SLOs. Operators manually assemble prefills, batch templates, and quant profiles for high-volume tenants which is error-prone and hard to scale. RampSmith is an autotuner that produces SKU-aware ramp plans, conservative prefill templates, and a set of quantization guidance (profiles and safety gates) to reduce unit economics for tenants while avoiding regressions in p95 latency and generation quality.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a new daemon: rampsmith-autotuner (service/rampsmith) responsible for tenant sampling, synthetic replay, cost/latency tradeoff search, and producing recommended artifacts (ramp plan, prefill template, quant hints).
- Introduces a compact ramp plan format (YAML/JSON) stored in tenant metadata that can be consumed by the deployment orchestrator to schedule burst capacity or tiered-prefill lanes.
- Implements a safe quant hints emitter that proposes per-tenant quant profiles with an automated rollback signal if generation quality metrics (perplexity proxy + fingerprint-preservation tests) degrade beyond thresholds.
- Console: new UI panel under Tenant > Economics to preview suggested plans, run a dry-run simulation, and accept/roll back the recommendation.
- Adds telemetry: new metrics to track estimated delta $/token, p95 latency delta, simulation pass/fail rates and rollback events.

Key design notes:
- Conservative defaults: by default RampSmith proposes only non-breaking, low-risk suggestions: micro-quant (8-bit fallback paths), smaller batching templates that do not increase p95 beyond configured SLO delta (default +10ms).
- Tenant isolation: recommendations are tenant-scoped and optionally gated behind tenant feature flags; global defaults are not overwritten automatically.
- Simulation-first workflow: recommendations include a simulation score computed from our synthetic replay engine (uses a 7-day sample of tenant traces). A recommendation must pass a simulation threshold to be promoted from draft -> recommended.
- Safety gates: include regression thresholds (latency, generation divergence) and automated rollback task that triggers a canary rollback if a configured metric breaches runtime tolerances.

Commit summary:
- feat(rampsmith): initial autotuner service and CLI scaffolding
- feat(rampsmith): tenant sampler, replay adapter, and search loop
- feat(rampsmith): compact ramp plan schema and persistence APIs
- feat(ui): tenant econ panel and preview/dry-run UI
- feat(telemetry): new metrics and Prometheus exporters
- test: end-to-end simulation tests + unit tests for search heuristics
- ci: add rampsmith integration job to canary pipeline

Changed files (high level):
- service/rampsmith/main.go (entrypoint + config)
- service/rampsmith/search/optimizer.go (search loop and heuristics)
- service/rampsmith/sim/replayer.go (synth replay adapter)
- internal/tenancy/metadata_store.go (store ramp plan pointers)
- webapp/src/tenants/EconomicsPanel.tsx (UI preview & dry-run)
- charts/rampsmith-prometheus-rules.yaml (alerting for rollbacks & regressions)
- tests/rampsmith/e2e_sim_test.go (integration simulation harness)
- docs/tenants/rampsmith.md (operator guide)
- .github/workflows/rampsmith-canary.yml (CI integration)

Testing and benchmarks:
- Unit tests: optimizer heuristics, persistence, and CLI validations (100% coverage on new logic).
- E2E simulation: ran synthetic replay for three representative tenants (chat, summarization, embeddings-heavy) across 72-hour traces: median estimated cost reduction 19%, p95 latency impact +3ms (within default tolerance).
- Canary: deployed to canary cluster for 48 hours with sampling; no rollbacks triggered; smoke monitoring checked generation divergence using fingerprint-based hashes.

Review conversation (abridged):
- Priya Nandakumar (reviewer): "Can we make sure the default simulation window is configurable and not accidentally trigger on short spikes? Also add a clear opt-out for tenants."
- Author (Ava): "Addressed: added config.SimulationWindow (default 7d) and tenant metadata flag tenant.econ.opt_out. Updated docs and UI to expose opt-out."
- Mateo Ruiz (reviewer): "Optimizer seems to prefer quantization aggressively for embeddings-heavy tenants; add a quality proxy check to prevent embedding skew."
- Author: "Added embedding-skew detector (sim/quality_checker.go) which compares centroid shift and blocks quant proposals if centroid shift > threshold. Threshold is controllable by operator."
- Liam Chen (approver): "Verified integration tests and canary metrics. Minor nits left around log verbosity and error messages."
- Author: "Addressed nits; reduced rampsmith info logs and added structured error codes."

CI status: all checks passed after two reruns. The new canary workflow triggered separate integration testing and was green. The lint workflow flagged an unused import in the first commit; fixed in the second commit.

Migration / operator notes:
- Feature is gated behind tenant feature flag `rampsmith_enabled` and cluster flag `features.rampsmith`. Defaults: off for all tenants. Operators must opt-in tenants or enable cluster-wide pilot before recommendations are applied automatically.
- Backup: ramp plans are stored in tenant metadata with versioning; rolling back to previous plan is supported.
- Resource note: the simulation job can be CPU/memory intensive for long windows; recommended default cadence for automated scans is once per 24–72 hours depending on cluster size.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge behind feature flag (this PR).
2) Enable for internal tenants and run 72h canary.
3) Open pilot for beta customers with SRE/product coordination.
4) Gradual opt-in for broader tenants after monitored success.

Security & compliance:
- No tenant secrets are exported. All analytics run against sampled, anonymized traces.
- Added RBAC checks to the UI endpoint; only users with "tenant.econ.manage" permission can accept plans.

Why this is different from existing econ work:
- Focused on tenant SKU ramping: producing actionable ramp schedules and conservative prefill templates rather than global default matrices.
- Simulation-first, conservative proposals with embedding-skew detector and automated rollback orchestration.

Follow-ups (future PRs):
- Auto-schedule execution hooks to wire ramp plans into Dedicated capacity autoscaler.
- ML-driven search policy that learns tenant-specific response surfaces over time.
- Exporter to generate tenant-level cost reports for finance reconciliation.

Files attached in this PR (representative snippets):
- service/rampsmith/search/optimizer.go: includes the hill-climb search with candidate scoring by expected dollar delta and latency penalty.
- webapp/src/tenants/EconomicsPanel.tsx: preview UI with a dry-run simulation chart and accept/rollback buttons.

ACKs / approvals:

Merge outcome:
